tagline: The northern end of the European shore — where the city gives way to forest, fishing villages, and some of Istanbul's finest seafood.

items.name: Sarıyer İskelesi Café
items.description: A simple café by the ferry landing with views of the Bosphorus and the fishing boats. Classic Turkish breakfast done well.

items.name: Büyükdere Sahil Cafés
items.description: A string of waterfront cafés along the Büyükdere coast, perfect for a relaxed morning with sea views.

items.name: Sarıyer Börekçisi
items.description: Famous throughout Istanbul for their freshly baked börek (flaky pastry with cheese, spinach, or meat). A must-stop.
items.tip: The cheese and spinach börek is the classic. Eat it hot straight from the oven.

items.name: Yosun Restaurant
items.description: Excellent fish restaurant in Sarıyer with Bosphorus views. Much less touristy than central Istanbul options at comparable quality.

items.name: Rumelikavağı Balık Restoranları
items.description: The fishing village of Rumelikavağı at the mouth of the Bosphorus has a row of outstanding fish restaurants. A proper day trip destination.
items.tip: Take the Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü all the way to the last stop. The journey is half the experience.

items.name: Belgrad Forest
items.description: A vast forest north of the city with hiking trails, picnic areas, and Ottoman-era water reservoirs. A true escape from urban life.
items.tip: Best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. The reservoir walk is the most scenic route.

items.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum
items.description: One of Istanbul's finest private art museums, set in a stunning villa on the Bosphorus with changing international exhibitions.

items.name: Emirgan Park
items.description: A beautiful Ottoman park famous for its tulips in April, but lovely year-round. Great café kiosks and Bosphorus views.
items.tip: The tulip festival in April is spectacular but extremely crowded. Autumn is equally beautiful and far quieter.

tips: Sarıyer is the end of the metro M2 line — the easiest part of Istanbul to reach by public transport from the city centre.
The Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü to Rumelikavağı is one of Istanbul's great experiences. Take it at least once.
Belgrad Forest is best reached by taxi from Sarıyer metro (about 15 min). Not walkable from the station.
The neighbourhood feels genuinely local — far fewer tourists than central areas.
